summary: Blind three-lens judgement of 76 figure labels whose MT changed when labels were joined, plus an independent recount of the headline numbers

result.method: I judged all 76 items blind, working only from items.json. I used books/efnafraedi-2e/glossary/glossary-unified.json as the terminology reference, and ran grep -a counts over efnafraedi-2e/02-mt-output to see which forms the corpus actually uses. I did not open any key, results or figure-text files. Rules I applied the same way on every item: (1) 'Moles of X' as 'Mólfjöldi X' is correct, bare 'Mól X' is correct and matches 'Massi X', and 'Mól af X' is acceptable because a teacher would likely tidy the 'af'. (2) An arrow label as an infinitive (Deila/Margfalda) or participle (Deilt/Margfaldað) is correct; an imperative (Deilið/Margfaldaðu/Margfaldið) is acceptable. (3) A letter or symbol joined to a noun takes a hyphen, so 'K-atóma' is correct and 'K atóma' acceptable. (4) Wrong-sense words are wrong: Þáttur for element, Vara for product, viðbrögð for reaction, and Stöðugleikastuðull or Stöðumælingarstuðull for stoichiometric factor.

Missing hyphen in 'X-atóm' is rated acceptable because the book hyphenates 215 times against 39 spaced.

result.method: Read all 76 items grouped by figure, using each figure's other labels to see what the label is for. Judged each candidate as printed figure text: case and inflection (genitive after units and in 'Mól X-atóma'), hyphenation of symbol compounds, whether a compound is written as one word, how an arrow instruction is phrased, and whether a pupil could misread it. I kept the same rule on every flowchart arrow: the plural imperative (Deilið/Margfaldið) and the participle (Deilt/Margfaldað) count as correct; the infinitive (Deila/Margfalda) and the singular imperative (Margfaldaðu) count as acceptable. Terms were checked against books/efnafraedi-2e/glossary/glossary-unified.json and word counts from grep -a over the chemistry 02-mt-output and 03-faithful-translation folders. I did not open any key, results, figure-text or run files.

recount.splitSurvival: 62 of 62 joined answers (J1 31/31, J2 31/31) split on '\n' into exactly the right number of non-empty lines. Scope: 31 figures with more than one label, 166 labels. The 3 single-label figures (brain-ec0b, basehyd_img, GreenChem) have no J requests and are left out. I checked that every J request's `keys` equals the P keys in idx order, and that its `en` equals the P `en` values joined with newlines.
recount.perLabelVsCommittedDiffer: 13 of 166 labels differ between P and the committed blocks, whether compared exactly or with whitespace normalised. Every one is a wording or inflection choice. Examples: aspirin 'Quantity' is 'Magn' in P and 'Fjöldi' committed; exocytosis 'Neuron' is 'Taugafruma' in P and 'Taugungur' committed; 'Deilið' vs 'Deila' (x2); moleratio2 'Sameindir CO2' vs 'CO2-sameindir'. No committed value was missing and no key is repeated within a figure.
recount.joinedRun1VsRun2Differ: 17 of 166 labels differ between J1 and J2 (the same count exactly or with whitespace normalised). 5 of the 17 are 'Stoichiometric factor', which came back in 5 different forms across the two runs: Stöðugleikastuðull, Stökiómetrískur þáttur, Stöðumælingarstuðull, Magnhlutfallsstuðull, Stökiómetrískur stuðull and Efnamagnsstuðull. P gave 'Efnajöfnustuðull' every time. The others are 'Mól af X' vs 'Mólfjöldi X', 'A-atóma' vs 'A atóma', imperative vs infinitive verb forms, 'Taugafruma' vs 'Taugungur', and 'sem þarf' vs 'þarf'.
recount.joinedVsPerLabelDiffer: J1 differs from P on 72 of 166 labels, and J2 differs from P on 72 of 166 (the same figures exactly or with whitespace normalised).
recount.stableJoinedChange: 59 of 166 labels have J1 == J2 != P. The biggest groups: 'Element' is 'Frumefni' in J and 'Þáttur' in P (5 figures); 'Molecular mass' is 'Sameindamassi' in J and 'Mólmassi' in P (3); 'Average atomic mass' is 'Meðal atómmassi' in J (4); 'Mól af X' in P became 'Mól X' or 'Mólfjöldi X' in J (about 15); 'Product' is 'Myndefni' in J and 'Vara' in P; 'Density' is 'Eðlismassi' in J and 'Þéttleiki' in P; 'Empirical formula' is 'Empírísk formúla' in J and 'Reynsluformúla' in P. Two stable J changes look like regressions: map2 'Stoichiometric factor' became 'Stöðugleikastuðull' ('stability factor'), and 'Percent CaSO4' became 'Hlutfall CaSO4'. The full list is printed by the script.
recount.formulaOrNumberDamage: None in any arm (P, J1, J2) or in the committed values. Method: for each of the 166 English labels I pulled out chemical formula tokens (element runs with parentheses, (aq)/(s)/(l)/(g) states and +/– charges), numbers (decimal comma counted as equal to a decimal point) and the symbols + – = → % × /, and compared them as counts against each Icelandic answer. 95 of the 166 English labels contain at least one such token. As a check, a deliberately altered string (C8H18→C8H17, 9.55→9,56) was flagged, and 12,85 was accepted as 12.85. The only hit was 'We' in 'We can make:', which my pattern mistook for a formula; it is not damage. All formulas survived, including Mg(ClO4)2, C7H5NO3S, CH3COO–, H3O+(aq), mol–1→mól–1 and 12.85→12,85, and the 10-space gap in both HClsoln equations was kept. One thing outside the formula check: 'mL' became 'ml' in both Example2_img labels in every arm and in the committed values (a unit case change, not mol→mól).
recount.billed: 90.88 in total from usage.cost across all 231 requests (the file does not name a currency). 9088 characters billed, at 0.01 per character. By arm: P 29.58 (2958 characters, 169 requests, including the 3 single-label figures), J1 30.65 (3065 characters, 31 requests), J2 30.65 (3065 characters, 31 requests). The billed character count is lower than len(en) on some requests (HClsoln, flowchart, map2), which looks like runs of spaces being collapsed before billing.
